novelty_reviews.verdict_reason: The claim (distributed GNN training algorithm DSGNN) combines five distinctive technical features: (1) leader-worker mode, (2) leader performing edge-segmentation-based graph flow partition, (3) worker mini-batch training based on graph summarization, (4) result return through an attention layer, and (5) leader-aggregated gradient computation with synchronous model updates. The two retrieved works both address only the generic object concept of distributed GNN training at scale. AGL (wrk_ff5aa18cf0cfe7be1ba5e8bd) uses a parameter-server architecture with k-hop neighborhood subgraph generation—not a leader-worker mode, not graph summarization, no edge-based graph flow partition, and no attention-layer result return. AliGraph (wrk_e59b8b7248dcc080455b8690) uses distributed graph storage and optimized sampling—no graph summarization, no leader-worker mode with edge-based partition, no attention-layer result return, and no leader-aggregated synchronous updates. Neither work discloses the claimed feature combination in whole or in combination, so the specific DSGNN technical solution is not revealed by the traceable prior art.
